title: Model what `git reset` does to the three trees
acceptanceCriteria: Every mode moves the current branch to the target and keeps `HEAD` on that branch
`--soft` leaves the index and working tree alone: the undone changes show as staged
`--mixed` resets the index to the target and leaves the working tree alone
`--hard` makes the index and every tracked file match the target
`--hard` leaves untracked files in the working tree
`--hard HEAD` discards staged and unstaged work, including a file that was only ever staged
No commit is deleted: `ORIG_HEAD` and the reflog lead back to the old tip, and resetting to it undoes the reset
The repo passed in is not modified
